speaker: Unknown
en: This is a much warmer welcome than what we had coming into Y Combinator the first time.
zh: 这比我们第一次进入 Y Combinator 时的欢迎要热烈得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Legora's YC journey started with a rejection, but more on that story later.
zh: Legora 的 YC 之旅始于一次拒绝，但稍后再详细说那个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: In YC, they teach you something, and it's called the two sentence description.
zh: 在 YC，他们会教给你一些东西，叫做两句话描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is describe your company in two sentences.
zh: 它是用两句话描述你的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Legora is the agentic operating system for lawyers, and it handles complex legal work from start to finish so lawyers can achieve more than ever before.
zh: Legora 是律师的智能体操作系统，它从头到尾处理复杂的法律工作，以便律师能够比以往取得更多成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: And over 3% of all the world's lawyers are now active users of Legora.
zh: 现在全球超过 3% 的律师是 Legora 的活跃用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will learn more about this when you get accepted into YC.
zh: 当你被 YC 录用时，你会了解更多关于这方面的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we started looking at the legal industry, it felt like one of the biggest opportunities to apply large language models to solve real problems.
zh: 当我们开始审视法律行业时，感觉这是应用大型语言模型解决实际问题最大的机会之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the software that we were up against looked like it had built in the 90s.
zh: 我们面对的软件看起来像是在 90 年代构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As software engineers, we have been incredibly spoiled with great software because we love to build for each other and for ourselves.
zh: 作为软件工程师，我们被优秀的软件极度宠坏了，因为我们喜欢为彼此和为自己构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the legal industry, this is what the software used to look like and what we were up against when we started out.
zh: 但在法律行业，这就是软件过去的样子，也是我们开始时面对的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, Legora has grown into a global brand, putting celebrities like Jude Law at the New York Wall Street.
zh: 现在，Legora 已经成长为一个全球品牌，让像 Jude Law 这样的名人出现在纽约华尔街。

speaker: Unknown
en: And still, I feel like we are only getting started.
zh: 尽管如此，我觉得我们才刚刚开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: My most favorite Slack channel in Legora is Customer Love.
zh: 我在 Legora 最喜欢的 Slack 频道是 Customer Love。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is where our customers post things that they...
zh: 这是我们的客户发布那些他们……

speaker: Unknown
en: sort of truly feel like they couldn't have achieved without our system.
zh: 有点真正觉得如果没有我们的系统就无法实现的事情的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we mine many of our sales calls for quotes like these.
zh: 我们从许多销售电话中挖掘像这样的语录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to share just a couple with you because I think at the end of the day, this is what it's all about.
zh: 我想给你们分享几个，因为我认为归根结底，这才是这一切的意义所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: A parent asked me at one of the tournaments how I juggle work and all of the golf travel.
zh: 在一次比赛中，一位家长问我如何平衡工作和所有的高尔夫旅行。

speaker: Unknown
en: One word, legora.
zh: 一个词，Legora。

speaker: Unknown
en: Never has the path between an idea and execute been so short.
zh: 从想法到执行之间的路径从未如此短暂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Never, man.
zh: 从未有过，伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: If Legora went away tomorrow, I'd just go back to coaching high school basketball.
zh: 如果 Legora 明天消失了，我就回去教高中篮球。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Legora went into YC, we were questioned about the idea of even selling and working in the legal industry.
zh: 当 Legora 进入 YC 时，我们被质疑关于在法律行业销售和工作的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is such a conservative business that had never been sort of lenient to software before.
zh: 这是一个如此保守的行业，以前从未对软件宽容过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from the time that we went into GA of October 2024 until the last end of quarter, we've grown from 1 to 100 million in ARR.
zh: 但从 2024 年 10 月我们进入 GA 到上个季度末，我们的 ARR 从 100 万增长到了 1 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And starting from just three engineers in Sweden to a company of over 750 people all over the world, this is awesome.
zh: 从瑞典的仅三名工程师起步，发展到如今遍布全球超过 750 人的公司，这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that we've gotten to do this starting from Europe, I think just adds another flair in that hat.
zh: 事实上我们从欧洲开始做这件事，我认为只是给那顶帽子增添了另一种风采。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the...
zh: 但那个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Legora's story almost didn't happen.
zh: Legora 的故事差点就没发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it actually didn't start with me.
zh: 它实际上并不是从我开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it started almost like the great beginning of a joke.
zh: 事实上，它几乎就像一个笑话的开端那样开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lawyer, a physicist, an engineer, and a psychologist, back in 2020, before GPT, before AI was cool, started a company called Judilica.
zh: 所以在 2020 年，在 GPT 之前，在 AI 变得酷之前，一位律师、一位物理学家、一位工程师和一位心理学家，创立了一家名为 Judilica 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they observed was that law school students were going into their internships basically to summarize court cases.
zh: 他们观察到的是法学院学生进入他们的实习期基本上是为了总结法庭案件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with the early models from Google called BERT, they started to explore what this space could be and what was possible to build.
zh: 利用 Google 的早期模型 BERT，他们开始探索这个空间可能是什么以及可以构建什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: My story started in the Swedish archipelago at an island which looks something like this.
zh: 我的故事始于瑞典群岛的一个看起来像这样的岛屿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I met my two co-founders at a volleyball game.
zh: 我在一次排球比赛中遇到了我的两位联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think startup founder stories can come from many different places, and this definitely wasn't one, you know, high odds of a place to start.
zh: 我认为创业者的故事可能来自许多不同的地方，这绝对不是一个你知道的，高概率的起步之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I met August and Sige, they showed me a demo of the product they had built, and our group chat actually looked exactly like this.
zh: 但当我遇到 August 和 Sige 时，他们给我展示了他们构建的产品演示，我们的群聊实际上看起来完全像这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: They gave me a demo of the project,
zh: 他们给我演示了那个项目，

speaker: Unknown
en: And with GPT 3.5, they had built a very simple product that could explain what a stock option agreement really meant.
zh: 利用 GPT 3.5，他们构建了一个非常简单的产品，可以解释股票期权协议的真正含义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started with that.
zh: 于是我们就从那开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, this is a super cool demo, a super cool project.
zh: 我说，这是一个超级酷的演示，一个超级酷的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my co-founder, Sige, said, I'm glad you want to help out.
zh: 我的联合创始人 Sige 说，我很想帮你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I ended up helping out a little bit more than just that.
zh: 我最后帮的忙比那多了一点点。

speaker: Unknown
en: When GPT 3.5 came, that was the internet moment of our generation.
zh: 当 GPT 3.5 到来时，那是我们这一代人的互联网时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I dropped out of college.
zh: 我从大学退学了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never finished my master thesis because the opportunity cost of not building had become too large.
zh: 我从未完成我的硕士论文，因为不去构建的机会成本已经变得太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when we started out, it wasn't obvious that we were going to be a success.
zh: 但当我们开始时，我们是否会成功并不明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to learn about what the legal industry was, what it meant, how lawyers actually worked, we came up with the ingenious plan of cold emailing lawyers on their emails that we could find on their websites and writing to them on LinkedIn asking for a lunch where we could learn more about their different practice areas.
zh: 因此，为了了解法律行业是什么，它意味着什么，律师实际上是如何工作的，我们想出了一个巧妙的计划，即在网站上找到的电子邮件地址给律师发冷邮件，并在 LinkedIn 上给他们写信，请求共进午餐，以便我们可以更多地了解他们不同的执业领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we offered to pay their hourly fee to have lunch with us.
zh: 我们提出支付他们的小时费来和我们一起吃午饭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of them took us up on that offer, but fortunately for us, many of them didn't make us pay for the hour, and many of them even paid for the lunch.
zh: 其中许多人接受了那个提议，但对我们来说幸运的是，许多人并没有让我们支付那笔小时费，甚至许多人还支付了午餐费。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once we had gotten our feet under ourselves, we approached one of the largest law firms in the Nordics named Mannheimer Swartling.
zh: 一旦我们站稳了脚跟，我们就去接触了北欧最大的律师事务所之一，名为 Mannheimer Swartling。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just two years before that, their managing partner had gone on TV and said that AI
zh: 但就在那两年前，他们的管理合伙人曾上电视并表示，AI

speaker: Unknown
en: Back when they were starting to use it, it was really more artificial than intelligent.
zh: 回顾他们刚开始使用它的时候，它真的是人工多于智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had to work really hard to change the perception of what both technology and what AI could be in the area of law.
zh: 所以我们必须非常努力地工作，以改变对技术以及 AI 在法律领域可能是什么的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In law, you are not paid when things go right, you are punished when things go wrong.
zh: 在法律界，事情做对时你不会得到报酬，事情出错时你会受到惩罚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of the initial AI solutions in the space had required immense amount of training.
zh: 而且该领域的许多最初的 AI 解决方案都需要大量的训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had to sort of bring a lot of use cases and examples just to get very, very little results.
zh: 你必须提供大量的用例和示例，才能得到非常非常少的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when GPT-3.5 came, that really changed the story.
zh: 而当 GPT-3.5 出现时，那真的改变了局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so with Mannheimer and Swartling, we ended up moving into their offices and working really close with them.
zh: 所以对于 Mannheimer and Swartling，我们最终搬进了他们的办公室，并与他们非常紧密地合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I said in the beginning, the warm welcome here was quite different from the first time we interacted with YC.
zh: 正如我一开始所说，这里的热烈欢迎与我们第一次与 YC 互动时截然不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: We applied in May of 2023 with a promise of being able to query all legal documents using large language models.
zh: 我们在 2023 年 5 月申请，承诺能够使用大语言模型查询所有法律文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we came to our interview, one of the first questions that we got asked was,
zh: 当我们来参加面试时，我们要问到的第一个问题之一是，

speaker: Unknown
en: What type of lawyers are you serving?
zh: 你们服务于哪类型的律师？

speaker: Unknown
en: And not very knowledgeable about the legal space yet, our response was, what do you mean?
zh: 而由于我们对法律领域还不是很了解，我们的回答是，你是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there different type of lawyers?
zh: 有不同类型的律师吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that did not land very well with the YC partners at the time.
zh: 这在当时并没有得到 YC 合伙人的很好反响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I actually remember very painfully that Tom Blomfield started laughing in the interview when we gave that response, and we knew that we were cooked.
zh: 所以我真的痛苦地记得，当我们给出那个回答时，Tom Blomfield 在面试中开始大笑，而且我们知道我们完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that also gave us the perseverance and the drive to continue.
zh: 但那也给了我们坚持下去的毅力和动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, with a lot of letdown, the day after we did not work, but the day after that, we got back to building.
zh: 所以，带着许多失落，我们没工作的那天之后我们没有工作，但再一天之后，我们回去继续构建了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two months later, we got accepted under a new name and with a different platform.
zh: 两个月后，我们以新名字和不同的平台被录取了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had done our homework, we had done the work, and...
zh: 我们做了功课，我们做了工作，而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: From Sweden, the idea of getting accepted into Y Combinator felt like we were going to Mount Olympus.
zh: 在瑞典，被 Y Combinator 录取的感觉就像我们要去奥林匹斯山。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were going to dine with the gods, and we were going to get to work with other startup founders who came from all of the great tech companies that we knew of.
zh: 我们将与诸神共餐，我们将有机会与我们知道的来自所有伟大科技公司的其他初创公司创始人一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once we got to Y Combinator, we realized that we actually knew a lot more than we thought we did.
zh: 一旦我们到了 Y Combinator，我们意识到我们实际上知道得比我们想象的多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is one of my favorite pictures.
zh: 这是其中一张我最喜欢的照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is the screenshot I took after we did the video call after our second YC interview when we knew that things had gone a lot better than the first time.
zh: 这是我在第二次 YC 面试后进行视频通话时截的屏，当时我们知道事情进展得比第一次好很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So after we got accepted into Y Combinator, we moved into this law firm I mentioned earlier, Mannheimer & Swartling.
zh: 所以在我们被 Y Combinator 录取后，我们搬进了我之前提到的这家律师事务所，Mannheimer & Swartling。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the biggest law firm in the Nordics, but they had no real clue about how to work with software and how to work with technology.
zh: 它是北欧最大的律师事务所，但他们对于如何与软件合作以及如何与科技合作完全没有真正的头绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we ended up getting a conference room with no real windows, where the AC would turn off at about 5 p.m., but it was really close to the Coke fridge.
zh: 我们最终得到了一间没有真正窗户的会议室，那里的空调大约在下午 5 点关掉，但它离可口可乐冰箱真的很近。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so at about 6 p.m. every day, one of the engineers would go up, grab the door, and start waving it back and forth to get more oxygen into the room.
zh: 所以每天大约下午 6 点，一位工程师会走过去，抓住门，开始来回摇晃它以让更多氧气进入房间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those conference chairs still made an imprint on all of our backs, I think, three years later.
zh: 而且那些会议椅在三年后依然在我们所有人的背上留下了印记，我想。

speaker: Unknown
en: And me in the car there with two more screens is when we make the move from the conference room of a law firm to our first real office.
zh: 那里车里的我和另外两块屏幕，是我们从律师事务所的会议室搬去我们第一个真正的办公室的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of the key takeaways from this entire experience is that first off, we quickly learned not to take no for an answer, but also the power of simply reaching out and asking for help.
zh: 我认为这次整个经历的关键要点之一是，首先，我们很快学会了不接受“不”作为答案，但也要学会仅仅通过伸出援手和寻求帮助的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one big lesson from these first three years of building Legora has been that it is very powerful to be a person and to be a company that others want to see succeed and that others want to help.
zh: 我认为在过去三年构建 Legora 的一个大教训是，做一个他人希望看到成功并想要帮助的人和公司是非常有力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we came to San Francisco.
zh: 所以我们来到了旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got a room at an Airbnb up in Bernal Heights, and we started building.
zh: 我们在 Bernal Heights 的 Airbnb 订了一个房间，然后我们开始构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: During YC, we grew from zero to a million dollars in ARR.
zh: 在 YC 期间，我们从零增长到了 100 万美元的 ARR。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also learned the hard way that working across San Francisco and Europe took a big toll on the team.
zh: 而且我们也惨痛地学到，在旧金山和欧洲之间跨地工作对团队造成了巨大的负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: I couldn't find a picture of this, but I bought a influencer ring light that I put on my laptop.
zh: 我找不到这张照片，但我买了一个网红环形灯放在我的笔记本电脑上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason I had that ring light was because I was doing sales calls between 1 a.m. in the morning
zh: 我有那个环形灯的原因是因为我在凌晨 1 点到……之间进行销售电话

speaker: Unknown
en: To 10 a.m. in the morning every single day in San Francisco to Europe because that was where our initial customer base was.
zh: （到）上午 10 点，在旧金山每一天向欧洲打，因为那里是我们最初的客户群所在地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after a rocket trajectory during YC, which now two years later is slow compared to what some of the companies are doing, we set off to fundraise.
zh: 在 YC 期间的火箭轨迹之后，现在两年后相比一些公司在做的事情来说显得缓慢了，我们出发去筹集资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was my first time fundraising.
zh: 这是我第一次筹集资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had no idea what to expect, but we had lined up 80 investor meetings in a week and a half, and we had European investors, American investors, and the main takeaway from that experience for me was that you need to become a really good storyteller in order to drive interest and to get people on your team.
zh: 我不知道该期待什么，但我们在一周半内安排了 80 场投资者会议，我们有欧洲投资者、美国投资者，那段经历给我的主要收获是，你需要成为一个非常好的讲故事的人，以驱动兴趣并让人们加入你的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was also a very different experience talking to some of the European investors versus some of the American investors.
zh: 与一些欧洲投资者交谈与和一些美国投资者交谈也是一种非常不同的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like in the US, we think more about what can go right rather than what could possibly go wrong.
zh: 我感觉在美国，我们更多地考虑什么会顺利，而不是考虑什么可能会出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we ended up working with a venture firm called Benchmark.
zh: 我们最终与一家名为 Benchmark 的风险投资公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a picture of Chetan, our partner, when we had signed the term sheets.
zh: 这是我们签署条款书时我们的合伙人 Chetan 的照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember negotiating that term sheet on his desk with a computer opened, going on decimals in the Excel to determine the exact number of shares.
zh: 我记得在他的桌子上谈判那张条款清单时，打开着一台电脑，在 Excel 里算到小数位以确定确切的股份数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they ended up investing $9.51 million.
zh: 他们最终投资了 951 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, following that investment, Redpoint pre-led our Series A just three weeks later.
zh: 现在，在那笔投资之后，红点资本仅仅三周后就预领投了我们的 A 轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started to run into a challenge.
zh: 我们开始遇到一个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had about $35 million on the bank.
zh: 我们在银行里大约有 3500 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were 10 people in the team.
zh: 我们团队里有 10 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was actually a month following that that we made more money from interest rates on those 35 million than we did from customers.
zh: 而在那之后实际上有一个月，我们从这 3500 万美元的利率上赚的钱比从客户那里赚的还多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is not a very good sign when you have become a bank.
zh: 当你变成一家银行时，这并不是一个很好的迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And going into our first board meeting,
zh: 在我们要去参加第一次董事会会议时，

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Chathan and we had Redpoint and it was me and my co-founders.
zh: 我们有 Chathan，我们有红点资本，那是我和我的联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we made a very hard decision, which was to freeze our sales motion.
zh: 我们做出了一个非常艰难的决定，就是冻结我们的销售动作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when you work with lawyers, you only really get one chance to get it right.
zh: 因为当你要和律师打交道时，你真的只有一次机会把它做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you show up and the product doesn't work,
zh: 如果你出现了而产品不工作，

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if the lag in the system is too high, or if the system goes down when there's too much traffic on your Azure instance, you are toast.
zh: 或者如果系统中的延迟太高，或者当你的 Azure 实例上有太多流量时系统崩溃了，你就完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after that six-month sales freeze was when we really started ripping.
zh: 而在那六个月的销售冻结之后，才是我们真正开始爆发的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where you see that curve from one million to 100 million really starting.
zh: 那就是你看到那条从一百万到一亿的曲线真正开始的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what happened at the start of that was,
zh: 而在开始时发生的事情是，

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, turning from a small startup looking for PMF to really establishing what our business and what our product was going to be.
zh: 你知道，从一家寻找 PMF 的小型初创公司转变为真正确立我们的业务和我们的产品将会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the very, very early days at LEIA, so even pre-LEGORA, the way that we would decide what to build was by voting.
zh: 在 LEIA 极早极早期，也就是甚至在 LEGORA 之前，我们决定构建什么的方式是通过投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would make democratic votes in the entire team.
zh: 我们会在整个团队中进行民主投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for anyone who has built software before, you know that if you have too many chefs in the kitchen, that typically does not make one very good dish.
zh: 对于任何以前构建过软件的人来说，你知道如果厨房里有太多的厨师，那通常做不出一道非常好的菜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was exactly what was going on.
zh: 而这正是当时正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were working on too many features.
zh: 我们正在做太多的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to rebuild everything for the product launch that we were going to have after the summer, after the sales freeze.
zh: 我们必须为我们要在夏天之后、在销售冻结之后举行的产品发布重建所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had to build a platform where
zh: 而我们不得不构建一个平台，在那里

speaker: Unknown
en: It was adaptable to foundations that were constantly changing, both with the underlying models, but also with the frameworks that we were using to build agentic workflows like LangChain, et cetera.
zh: 它能适应不断变化的基础，无论是底层模型，还是我们用来构建像 LangChain 等智能体工作流的框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: In October of 2024, we wrote down what we would call the Layup Product Manifesto.
zh: 2024 年 10 月，我们写下了我们要称为 Layup 产品宣言的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was basically gathering everything we had learned, putting it into one very simple document that we shared with the entire 25 strong person team back then, and that we would rally the troops around.
zh: 这基本上是收集我们学到的一切，把它放进一个非常简单的文档中，那时我们与整个 25 人的强大团队分享了它，并且我们将以此团结队伍。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, we were doing about $1.3 million in annual recurring revenue.
zh: 当时，我们的年度经常性收入大约是 130 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of our competitors were doing 10 times that with products that only had one of these features.
zh: 而我们的许多竞争对手做的是那个数字的 10 倍，而他们的产品只有这些功能中的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also think that's a function of having started in Sweden.
zh: 我也认为这是在瑞典起步的一个作用结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market is not big enough to house a real unicorn or a decahorn or something even bigger than that.
zh: 这个市场不够大，无法容纳一只真正的独角兽或者一只十角兽或者甚至比那更大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the earliest questions we got from YC was, when will you move to the United States?
zh: 所以我们从 YC 那里得到的最早的问题之一是，你们什么时候会搬到美国？

speaker: Unknown
en: When will you make the jump?
zh: 你们什么时候会进行跨越？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was off the back of this product refocus that we...
zh: 而正是基于这次产品的重新聚焦，我们...

speaker: Unknown
en: We're able to not only compete out the competition on product, but build enough momentum to make the jump over to the US and start to compete for the biggest logos in our markets.
zh: 能够不仅通过产品击败竞争，而且建立足够的势头跨越到美国，并开始为我们市场上最大的客户品牌而竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as engineers and as tech people, we often overemphasize the reliance on product and on the tech.
zh: 我认为作为工程师和作为技术人员，我们经常过度强调对产品和对技术的依赖。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if there's anything I've learned in these past three years, it's that it's all about the people.
zh: 但如果说我在过去三年里学到了什么，那就是这完全取决于人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And building product is one thing, but building a company is a very different thing.
zh: 构建产品是一回事，但构建公司是一件非常不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we made many early mistakes around this.
zh: 我们在这方面犯了很多早期的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the hiring patterns that we had to unlearn was looking for fancy logos on resumes or what we like to call why intercept.
zh: 我们不得不忘记的一种招聘模式是寻找简历上光鲜的公司标志，或者我们要称之为“why intercept”的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about somebody's skill curve, it might start out really high, but if they don't have a good trajectory upwards, they are going to have a really hard time working in a company that is scaling exponentially.
zh: 如果你考虑某人的技能曲线，它可能开始得很高，但如果他们没有一个良好的上升轨迹，他们将会在一家指数级扩张的公司里非常艰难地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so instead, we started to look for people like us who wanted to work insanely hard with a very high growth potential, and we doubled down on that talent over and over again.
zh: 因此相反，我们开始寻找像我们一样想要疯狂努力工作并且具有非常高增长潜力的人，并且我们一次又一次地把赌注押在那类人才上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our top seller today is 23 years old, and he sold over more than $10 million worth of Liguora.
zh: 我们今天的顶级销售员 23 岁，他卖了超过 1000 万美元的 Liguora。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he had no sales background.
zh: 他没有任何销售背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: He jumped out of university.
zh: 他从大学里跳了出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by continuously doubling down on that type of talent, I think we have built a very unique culture at Legora.
zh: 通过不断地在那类人才上加倍下注，我认为我们在 Legora 建立了一种非常独特的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of those things has been about bringing and building cultural fit.
zh: 其中一件事就是关于引进和构建文化契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Up until the point where we were around 500 people, I interviewed every single candidate outside of engineering.
zh: 直到我们大约有 500 人的时候，我面试了工程之外的每一位候选人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I interview every director and upwards.
zh: 现在我面试每一位董事及以上级别的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we have done is we have set the cultural foundation in the business where it self-selects for itself.
zh: 但我们所做的是我们在业务中建立了文化基础，在那里它能自我筛选。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have three values at Legora.
zh: 我们在 Legora 有三个价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lean in, fight for excellence, and grow together.
zh: 全情投入，追求卓越，共同成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And together they make LFG.
zh: 它们合起来构成了 LFG。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's fucking go.
zh: 让我们他妈的去干吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also sends a signal to leaders and others who join the company who are coming from more perhaps established backgrounds, where joining a company where the values includes profanity quickly sort of tells them what this is about.
zh: 这也向加入公司的领导和其他人发出了信号，他们可能来自更成熟的背景，加入一家价值观包含脏话的公司很快就能告诉他们这是关于什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another very complex cultural thing, starting a company in Scandinavia,
zh: 另一个非常复杂的文化问题，在斯堪的纳维亚创办公司，

speaker: Unknown
en: is something called Jantelagen, or the Law of Jante.
zh: 是叫做 Jantelagen 的东西，或者叫 Jante 法则。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is very foreign to our American friends, but in Swedish culture, this basically means that you should not think that you are somebody, or you are not more important than anybody else, and your ideas are not better than anybody else's.
zh: 这对我们的美国朋友来说很陌生，但在瑞典文化中，这基本上意味着你不应该认为你是个大人物，或者你并不比其他人更重要，而且你的想法并不比其他人的好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a part of this humility is good and it supports a culture where the best ideas win and where people earlier in their careers feel empowered to speak up.
zh: 我认为这种谦卑的一部分是好的，它支持一种最好的想法胜出的文化，以及职业生涯早期的人感到被赋权去发言的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's very hard to build one of the fastest growing enterprise companies in the world
zh: 但要建立世界上增长最快的企业公司之一是非常困难的

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think that you aren't somebody or if you don't think that you are better than anybody else.
zh: 如果你不认为你是个大人物或者如果你不认为你比其他人更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have had to really create a nice cocktail of US, European, and Asian culture all in one to create a global company that is Legor today.
zh: 因此我们确实必须创造一种包含美国、欧洲和亚洲文化的美妙鸡尾酒，以创造今天的 Legor 这家全球性公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I really think that building a strong company culture is the best guarantee to attract and keep the best people.
zh: 所以我真的认为建立强大的公司文化是吸引和留住最好的人的最佳保证。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another way that company culture gets expressed at Legora is through articles like this one that ended up in Sifted.
zh: 公司文化在 Legora 得以表达的另一种方式是通过像这样最终出现在 Sifted 上的文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, there is only winning.
zh: 对我们来说，只有赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything else is losing in a winner-takes-all market or winner-takes-most market.
zh: 在赢家通吃或赢家通吃大部分的市场中，其他一切都是输。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the company has to run like there is no place for number two.
zh: 公司必须像没有第二名立足之地那样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it actually would be fair to say that when Legora was founded, it really had no reason to exist.
zh: 我认为实际上可以说公平的是，当 Legora 成立时，它真的没有存在的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were one of many legal AI companies.
zh: 我们是众多法律 AI 公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But
zh: 但

speaker: Unknown
en: Because of this mentality and because of not feeling like we're safe, even though we have achieved extraordinary numbers by any normal measures, we continue acting like professional swimmers who are looking down in our lane while the competition is looking sideways at what we're doing.
zh: 因为这种心态，因为不觉得我们是安全的，尽管按照任何正常标准我们都取得了非凡的数字，我们继续表现得像职业游泳运动员一样看着我们的泳道，而竞争者则在侧视看我们在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Legora, we have had to build a culture to really support that ambition.
zh: 在 Legora，我们不得不建立一种文化来真正支持这种雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So starting years behind some of our biggest competition and having to build this intensity in a country where most people want to go for fika at 3 p.m., which means having a cinnamon bun and a coffee, or go home at 5, one of the ways that that has been done is to
zh: 所以落后于我们最大的竞争对手几年起步，并且不得不在一个大多数人想在下午 3 点去 fika 的国家建立这种强度，fika 意味着吃一个肉桂圆面包和喝咖啡，或者在 5 点回家，做到这一点的方法之一是

speaker: Unknown
en: Create cultural values and...
zh: 创造文化价值观以及……

speaker: Unknown
en: Cultural moments that really distinguish us from many others.
zh: 真正将我们与其他许多人区分开来的文化时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in Swedish, there is a saying, you can wake up with a taste of blood because you're so excited about something.
zh: 所以在瑞典语中，有一句谚语，你可以带着血腥味醒来，因为你对某事太兴奋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was doing an article in Swedish, and I used that saying.
zh: 我当时正在用瑞典语写一篇文章，我用了那个谚语。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't know that the interviewer was going to release that article in English.
zh: 而且我不知道采访者会发布那篇文章的英文版。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when this came out, it got lots of fun reactions.
zh: 所以当这出来时，它得到了很多有趣的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them was, is Legora made up of vampires?
zh: 其中一个是，Legora 是由吸血鬼组成的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The second one was, you guys need to floss better.
zh: 第二个是，你们需要更好地用牙线清洁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many good ideas, but this has now turned into the word blood smoke internally, which means that, and we just keep going at it.
zh: 很多好主意，但这现在在内部变成了 blood smoke 这个词，这意味着，而且我们只是在继续做下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think part of having our HQ in Stockholm has worked to help us keep this.
zh: 我认为将我们的总部设在斯德哥尔摩在某种程度上帮助我们保持了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody globally from the company makes their onboarding in Stockholm, which is a lot nicer in summer than in the winter.
zh: 全球公司的每个人都在斯德哥尔摩进行他们的入职培训，这比在冬天要在夏天好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that has created the same vibe in any Legora office, regardless of where you walk in all over the world.
zh: 但这在任何 Legora 办公室创造了同样的氛围，无论你在世界哪个地方走进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one great example of this was we had a very big law firm in the US that our competition was working with.
zh: 我认为一个很好的例子是我们有一家美国非常大的律师事务所，我们的竞争对手正在与之合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that law firm had a specific problem around being able to draft certain types of documents based on incoming term sheets.
zh: 但那家事务所在能够根据收到的条款清单起草某些类型的文档方面有一个特定问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our competition had promised that they were going to solve that problem for them, and they hadn't.
zh: 我们的竞争对手曾承诺他们会为他们解决那个问题，但他们没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of our US-based engineers, legal engineers, lawyers, learned about this use case, got on a flight to Stockholm, spent a week with our engineers, solved the problem in Sweden, and then went back to the US and delivered it to the customer.
zh: 所以我们的一位驻美国的工程师、法律工程师、律师，了解到了这个用例，坐上了飞往斯德哥尔摩的航班，花了我们工程师一周的时间，在瑞典解决了这个问题，然后回到美国并交付给了客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that...
zh: 我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Swedish base has become one of Legora's real superpowers.
zh: 瑞典基地已成为 Legora 真正的超能力之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to round things off before we jump into the Q&A, I'm sharing this stage this weekend with people who have built things at a scale that I haven't yet gotten close to.
zh: 所以在进入问答环节之前做个总结，这个周末我正在这个舞台上与那些以我尚未接近的规模构建事物的人分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I will leave many of the big lessons for them.
zh: 所以我会把许多重要的经验留给他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I can tell you is that three years in, it's a little bit smaller than that.
zh: 但我可以告诉你的是，三年后，这比那要小一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of what actually mattered in the company and in Legora so far did not revolve around signing a big client or...
zh: 迄今为止，在公司和 Legora 中大多数真正重要的事情并不围绕着签下一个大客户或者……

speaker: Unknown
en: Closing a new round of financing or open a new big office in Manhattan.
zh: 完成新一轮融资或在曼哈顿开设一个新的大办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: It happened in a windowless room without much oxygen or on a call on our way to the airport, a Slack channel at 2 a.m. trying to fix a bug before a big presentation on Monday.
zh: 它发生在一个没有多少氧气的无窗房间里，或者在去机场路上的电话里，在凌晨 2 点的 Slack 频道里试图在周一的大型演示之前修复一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nobody puts that in a pitch deck, but that is what makes the company.
zh: 没有人把那个放进融资演示文稿，但这正是成就公司的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You shouldn't wait around for those big moments.
zh: 你不应该等待那些大时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to love the hustle.
zh: 你得热爱这种拼搏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if I can leave you with anything, it's that even though we started in a small law firm in Sweden, I was born in the Swedish archipelago with a class of 10 other people.
zh: 我想如果我能给你留下点什么的话，那就是即使我们在瑞典的一家小律所起步，我出生在瑞典群岛，同届只有 10 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought I had a big plan for my life, and I was going to go to McKinsey after school.
zh: 我原以为我对自己的人生有一个大计划，我毕业后要去 McKinsey。

speaker: Unknown
en: When GPT 3.5 dropped in our knees, we truly made that into our thing, and we captured what I believe to be our generation's internet moment.
zh: 当 GPT 3.5 掉进我们的膝盖时，我们真的把它变成了我们的事业，并且我相信我们抓住了这一代人的互联网时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can just do things.
zh: 所以你们就可以做事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Legorah and myself is living proof of that.
zh: Legorah 和我自己就是活生生的证明。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that, we're going to jump to Q&A, and I want to invite a very good friend, our partner from Y Combinator, Gustav Omstrammer.
zh: 所以借此机会，我们将进入问答环节，我想邀请一位非常好的朋友，我们在 Y Combinator 的合伙人，Gustav Omstrammer。

speaker: Unknown
en: Christoph, we're really becoming professionals at this now.
zh: Christoph，我们现在真的成为这方面的专业人士了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not the first time we're doing this.
zh: 这不是我们第一次做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's great.
zh: 不，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's good to see you.
zh: 很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for the talk.
zh: 谢谢你的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was awesome.
zh: 那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really good.
zh: 真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And always thank you for coming back and speaking to YC and to founders here at Startup School.
zh: 并且总是感谢你回来并在这里对 YC 和 Startup School 的创始人们演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to ask the first question, which is one that I've gotten from a lot of founders who ask about you, which is you guys are three founders or were three founders who were not lawyers and you started the best legal AI company in the world.
zh: 我想问第一个问题，这也是很多问起你的创始人们问过我的问题，就是你们是三位或者曾经是三位不是律师的创始人，而且你们创办了世界上最好的法律 AI 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does domain expertise not matter that much anymore?
zh: 领域专业知识不再那么重要了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's actually a story of a Swedish VC who was very bullish on doing the pre-seed of Leia, but they ended up not doing it because we did not have any lawyers in the team.
zh: 所以实际上有一个瑞典 VC 的故事，他非常看好做 Leia 的种子轮前，但他们最终没有做，因为我们的团队里没有任何律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I met them at the airport.
zh: 我在机场见到了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I met one of the partners from there at the airport quite recently, and they were very, very bitter.
zh: 我最近在机场见了那里的一位合伙人，他们非常、非常痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Leia or Legora turned out to be the lesson for them that perhaps domain expertise is not what you need to succeed.
zh: 而且 Leia 或 Legora 对他们来说成了一个教训，也许领域专业知识并不是你成功所需要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that you need a willingness to learn about the market, which...
zh: 我认为你需要有学习市场的意愿，这……

speaker: Unknown
en: We did very, very early by exposing ourselves and spending lots of time with lawyers, as much as we possibly could.
zh: 我们非常、非常早地通过让自己接触律师并尽可能多地花时间与律师在一起来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't think you need domain expertise, probably dependent on the market that you're going after.
zh: 但我不认为你需要领域专业知识，这可能取决于你所追求的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe if you're building in quantum computing or in fusion, that's a good idea.
zh: 也许如果你在做量子计算或聚变，那是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But legal was easy enough for us to pick up as we went along.
zh: 但法律对我们来说很容易，我们在进行中就学会了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spoke to some founders yesterday, and we spoke about the next categories where the LLMs are not sufficiently good yet, but they will be.
zh: 我昨天和一些创始人谈过，我们谈到了下一个类别，其中 LLMs 还不够好，但它们会好的。

en: In a way, I think...
zh: 在某种程度上，我认为……

en: Most of the work up until that point makes you qualified for that thing.

en: Right.

en: You get to the next minigame by basically seeing the last one.

en: Yes, but you need to make sure that you learn because part of every minigame.
zh: 是的，但你需要确保你学习，因为这是每个小游戏的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you really need to...
zh: 而且我认为你真的需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: Put the company first, way ahead of your own ego in a way.
zh: 把公司放在第一位，在某种程度上远超你自己的自我。

en: And I tell this to the executive team, I need to re-qualify for the job as CEO of Legora every quarter.

en: And I think for myself, if you

speaker: Unknown
en: And then...
zh: 然后……

en: I think, as always, you try to build a good network of people who have done it before.
zh: 我认为，一如既往，你尝试建立一个由以前做过此事的人组成的优质人脉网络。

en: The tough thing is there's very few people who have done the company this quickly as we are.
zh: 困难之处在于，很少有人像我们一样如此迅速地把公司做成这样。

en: And even a lot of the executives that we are now bringing on, they come from a sauce.
zh: 甚至我们现在引进的很多高管，他们都来自一个酱汁。

en: And they come from this world of triple, triple, double, double.
zh: 他们来自这个三三、双双的世界。

en: You're sort of on track.

en: That's not enough anymore.

en: And so you need to just compress timelines.
zh: 所以你只需要压缩时间线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious how you get Jude Law to be the face of the company.
zh: 我很好奇你是如何请到裘德·洛成为公司形象的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you haven't seen the ads, I recommend you go into YouTube and watch the Legora Jude Law ads.
zh: 如果你还没看过这些广告，我建议你去 YouTube 上看看 Legora 裘德·洛的广告。

en: Did you fall in love with law again?

en: Yeah, I did.
zh: 是的，我爱上（法律）了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good.

en: What happened?

en: How did you score that?

en: OK, so the inside baseball is...

en: We had a meeting with one of our marketing agencies, and one of their pitches was, why don't we redo very famous legal scenes?
zh: 我们要和我们的营销代理公司开了一个会，他们中的一个提案是，为什么不重拍非常著名的法律场景？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you can't handle the truth?
zh: 比如，“你承受不住真相”？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why don't we redo famous legal scenes with lawyers, but with Liguara?
zh: 为什么不重拍律师的著名法律场景，但是用 Liguara？

speaker: Unknown
en: The pitch was this.
zh: 提案是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually pretty funny.
zh: 实际上挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of these movies about lawyers, like what if they just had Legora and the movie would be over in like a minute.
zh: 所有这些关于律师的电影，比如如果他们只有 Legora，电影就会在一分钟内结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we got to this idea of working with actors.

en: And then somebody went, well, Legora is like AI-powered law.

en: What if we got Jude Law to be like AI-powered?
zh: 如果我们请裘德·洛来代表 AI 驱动的会怎样？

en: And that got us down the track of like, huh, maybe we could get Jude Law.

speaker: Unknown
en: And he thought we were completely unserious when we reached out the first time, like some Swedish AI company wants to work with Jude Law to make billboards and a campaign.
zh: 当我们第一次联系他时，他以为我们完全不正经，就像一些瑞典 AI 公司想和裘德·洛合作做广告牌和宣传活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we were so persistent, and I think one underappreciated form of negotiation is nagging.
zh: 但我们非常坚持，我认为一种被低估的谈判形式就是唠叨。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the things my dad taught me.
zh: 这是我爸爸教我的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we nagged and nagged and nagged, and he said yes.
zh: 我们唠叨了又唠叨，然后他说了行。

en: On one condition, he got to pick his own scriptwriter and cinematographer.
zh: 在一个条件下，他可以选择自己的编剧和电影摄影师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And who would have known?
zh: 谁能知道呢？

zh: 他们基本上进了片场，Liguara 的人都不允许进入。

en: And a few hours later, these magical productions come out.
zh: 几个小时后，这些神奇的作品就出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really good.
zh: 真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so funny.

zh: 这真的令人兴奋。

en: Awesome.
